newsitem.title: USA: AEP agrees power contract with AK Steel.
newsitem.headline: AEP agrees power contract with AK Steel.

text.p: American Electric Power (AEP) said Wednesday it has agreed to sell electricity and other services to an alliance of companies serving a new AK Steel Holding steel plant near Rockport, Ind.

Under the terms of a four-year wholesale agreement, AEP will provide more than 100 megawatts of electricity delivered to the alliance's new 765,000-volt interconnection with the AEP system, the company said in a statement.

The alliance of companies includes SIGCORP Inc subsidiary Southern Indiana Gas and Electric Co, and Hoosier Energy Rural Electric Cooperative member Southern Indiana Rural Electric Cooperative, AEP said.
Under the agreement, AEP will begin providing the electricity in early 1998.

AEP also said subsidiary AEP Resources Engineering & Services Co has a separate agreement with AK Steel to build a substation for the Rockport mill that will be capable of receiving 765,000-volt electricity from the transmission grid.
"To our knowledge, this will be the first industrial customer of any utility in North America with the capability to receive electricity at 765,000 volts," AEP Resources said.
Construction of the substation is underway and is expected to be completed by March 1, 1998.
